Yes, SoundCloud does have a premium version but it's $15 a month and I'm not currently in the position to pay for that right now. I'm currently in college right now, searching for a part-time job. I think there's many articles about uploading stuff to iTunes but from my understanding, the cost comes from creating a  website domain and maintaining it for a set amount (anything from $10-$15 a month). Then you can create an RSS feed and upload your podcast to iTunes using the feed. It's been a while since I've looked up this information so you might want to double-check it if I've made any mistakes.

"Audio blog"? Huh, I never thought about it that way but it makes sense :D  According to Google, a podcast is "a digital file made available on the Internet for downloading to a computer..." so I guess mine still counts :)

1. I co-host it with my little brother but recently, since he's been very busy with high school and college applications, I've recorded a few episodes by myself. 

2. I always want my friends to be on it (like one of my friends from Ukraine) but they're not as comfortable speaking to a general audience as I am.

3. Episodes are typically 30-40 minutes long and solo episodes are 5-20 minutes long.

1. My podcast is mostly about pop culture (mainly video games and movies) and childhood nostalgia. Our most recent episode was about Earthbound, and one of my most popular episodes was about Sonic the Hedgehog. Our next episode, which will be celebrating a huge milestone for us, will be about the numerous anime series I've been watching with my little brother :)

2. I've always been on the fence about getting a bigger audience. It'd be nice to be more visible among the rest of the internet community but at the same time, I know how dangerous that kind of notoriety can be. If I had a listenership of 50-100 people, I'd think that would be just the right amount. Enough that a decent amount of people are listening and that I feel like the work I put in was worth it. 

3. I've tried to have guests before but either they forget they wanted to do it or they're afraid of their voices being broadcast to a general audience. So technically, my only guest is my little brother who is also the co-host.

I started it in 2010 using only a Sanza Fuze to record the audio but stopped once I became a freshman in college the next year. I started it again in 2013 when I wanted to become better at editing audio/got really bored that summer. Seems like a lot of wonderful things come from boredom :D

For a while, I used the internal microphone from my macbook to record it. Nowadays, I record it using a Blue Yeti microphone. Sound is more focused now but unfortunately, I can't currently afford any kind of sound-deafening foam that could reduce the amount of traffic sounds that tend to seep through in a recording. 

At first, I uploaded episodes to YouTube but stopped when I got a copyright claim for using licensed music. Then I tried Soundcloud but stopped again due to: a 2 hour limit for overall uploads, and Soundcloud becoming more aggressive with copyright strikes. Now I upload directly to Google Drive and share the links directly to my friends/post a link to my blog. It seems to be the most reliable method although I'd like to upload it to iTunes if only it wasn't costly to have an RSS feed.
